dedupe_keys.name: nature based solutions for urban flooding in 58 us public parks li and guo land 2024

description: This case study examines how 58 public parks in major US cities use nature-based solutions to manage urban flooding. Jiayang Li and Ziyi Guo of the University of Florida's College of Design, Construction and Planning published it in Land in September 2024, drawing on a 2022 survey by the Trust for Public Land and secondary datasets. They build a typology of park NBS in five high-level categories by size and capacity, position on the grey to green spectrum and design objective, and relate each park's adopted types to its landscape and sociodemographic context. Ecosystem-based measures were the most common and engineered infiltration features without living elements the least; parks with ecosystem-based measures had more surrounding greenspace and higher flood risk, while links to neighbourhood income, poverty, race and age were suggestive but not significant. Coverage is 58 parks. Format and access: an open access article. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: the sample follows one survey and does not measure flood reduction. It informs design and siting of park-based green-blue infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the Landscape Performance Series briefs and the NYC Green Infrastructure Program.
